item.title: milind-soni/OpenMausBot
item.description:
Open-source Grok Bot alternative with a virtual machine that bots can use

https://www.mausbot.com/

OpenMausBot

The open-source Grok Bot alternative: your own team of AI bots, in a chat app.

openmausbot.com  ·  Download  ·  Open source Grok Bot alternative, compared

OpenMausBot is an open-source Grok Bot alternative: an independent project inspired by Grok Bot, and the open-source alternative to Meta Muse, OpenAI dots and Cue by Manus — bring-your-own-agent, local-first, on the models you already have. Also known as MausBot; formerly OpenGrokBot. Not affiliated with xAI, Meta, OpenAI or Manus.

Every bot in the sidebar is a real agent — Claude or Codex running locally under the hood — with its own personality, its own model, its own cloud computer, and its own connected apps. Talk to them like contacts. Watch them work. Approve what matters.


     

latest release  ·  macOS: Apple silicon & Intel · signed & notarized .dmg  ·  Windows: x64 installer  ·  Ubuntu 24.04 x64: .deb or AppImage beta  ·  Fedora x64: .rpm  ·  all releases




Powered by boat.dev



Inference provider sponsor



⚠️ No affiliation with any cryptocurrency. OpenMausBot has no token. Any coin using the OpenMausBot, Maus, or SupaMaus name is not created, endorsed, or affiliated with this project or its maintainer. I have received no tokens, payment, or allocation from anyone, and I will not be endorsing any token.

Why

One assistant in one box is the wrong shape for agents. OpenMausBot is an independent, open-source project inspired by Grok Bot — it keeps the idea (AI as a messaging app: a roster of bots you chat with, each with its own personality, memory of its thread, model, computer, and apps) and rebuilds it open, local-first, and on the agents you already have:

  • Bring your own agents. Bots run on the claude, codex, and grok CLIs installed on your own machine — your existing logins and subscriptions, no new accounts, no proxy in the middle. Point any engine at a custom CLI binary (a versioned build or wrapper) in Settings → Engines.
  • Local first. One small harness server on 127.0.0.1 owns every agent process. Transcripts, keys, and events live in ~/.openmausbot, not a cloud.
  • Agents with hands. Each bot can use a cloud Linux desktop, an isolated Local VM, or—where the platform safety boundary is currently certified—your own computer, plus 500+ apps through Composio. Host control is available on macOS and Ubuntu Xorg after explicit opt-in. Ubuntu Wayland host control remains disabled while issue #345 is resolved.

The open-source alternative to Grok Bot, Muse, dots and Cue

Four closed personal-agent products shipped in seven weeks of 2026, and each one keeps the model, the computer and your data on its maker's side of the line. OpenMausBot is the open-source version of that shape: a team of agents in a chat app, each with its own model, its own computer and its own connected apps, running on your machine under Apache 2.0. If you searched for an open Muse, open dots, an open-source Grok Bot, an open Instinct or an open Cue, this is the repository.

Looking for What it is How OpenMausBot differs Read more
Open source Grok Bot xAI's roster of bots on one shared cloud computer, Grok only, from a SuperGrok or Cursor plan Same roster shape; any model per bot; your own machine; approval cards Grok Bot vs OpenMausBot
Open Muse Meta's single personal agent in a Meta cloud VM, US and Canada only A team instead of one agent; runs anywhere; data in ~/.openmausbot Meta Muse alternative
Open dots OpenAI's always-on agent inside ChatGPT, GPT only, Pro and Business Premium plans Several agents; your Claude, ChatGPT or Grok login; no plan required OpenAI dots alternative
Open Cue Manus's invite-only agents with their own phone, email and wallet No invite; OAuth instead of passwords; open source Cue by Manus alternative
Open Instinct Spear Street's invite-only agent that holds your passwords on a cloud computer Ask for approval when you want it; signs in over OAuth; your machine Instinct AI alternative

All five side by side: Muse vs Grok Bot vs Dots vs Cue, and a decision guide in five questions: Which AI agent should I use?

Features

🧠 Pick a brain per bot

A model picker with a provider rail — Claude and Codex models side by side, defaults marked, unavailable providers dimmed with the reason. Switch a bot's model mid-conversation.

🖥️ Every bot gets a computer

Open the Computer panel and the bot's cloud desktop spins up on its own — live screen preview while it works, "Open desktop" to take over in your browser, or point the bot at this Mac instead.

🙋 Bots ask before they act

Shell commands, file edits, and questions surface as inline cards — Allow / Deny / answer in chat. A permission broker turns every risky action into a decision you make, for cloud and local computers alike.

🔌 Connected apps

A one-click marketplace over Composio Sessions: Gmail, Slack, GitHub, Notion, Linear and hundreds more. OAuth once, and every bot can use them as tools.

🗂 Manage bots like chats

Right-click any bot: pin, mark unread, edit profile, duplicate, copy conversation ID, hide, delete. It's a messaging app — your agents behave like contacts.

🔑 Keys once, everything lights up

Paste credentials in App Settings — they persist locally and the provider fleet hot-reloads instantly. Secrets are write-only: the UI only ever sees "configured" flags.

#️⃣ Channels for every context

Keep Work, Personal, and each project in separate channels without cloning your bots. Every channel has its own transcript, shared instructions, working folder, responder rules, and editable bot roster. File a channel and its bots under a named context, then rename it or change its members whenever the team changes.

⚡ Fast decisions with Jev

Add a Cloudflare Workers AI token with its account ID, a TypeSafe Jev key, or an OpenRouter key and model, in Settings › AI › Routing and extraction and rooms set to Auto pick the bot that fits each un-mentioned message in a few hundred milliseconds, falling back to the room's lead whenever the decision model is off or unsure. See docs/decision-model.md.

📦 Install a complete team from one Markdown file

Browse outcome-driven teams on BotMRR, then choose Add to OpenMausBot. The app opens a review screen before creating the bots, Chief of Staff, channels, playbooks, connector checklist, and suggested routines. You can also import the same .md file from disk or paste its public GitHub URL in Teams → Import.

The format stays portable: OpenMausBot reads the structured YAML frontmatter for a reliable one-click install, while Grok, Claude, ChatGPT, and people can follow the ordinary Markdown playbook. Connections remain off until you approve them, routines arrive paused, and packages never carry credentials, conversations, permissions, memory, or computer access. Browse the open-source playbook repository or read its portable format.

🤝 Share a bot or a department

Ask a bot to share itself ("publish yourself to GitHub"), or open a department's … menu and choose Share. You get one card: the bots, their instructions, skills and pictures, group chats, routines (paused), the Chief of Staff and the apps they use, by name. Chats, memory, keys and connection addresses never go in. Publish sends it to the community repository on GitHub and gives you a link; Save folder… keeps it on your computer. Anyone adds it with + → Import… and a link or a folder. See docs/team-sharing.md. Desktops connected to an organization also get the packages its Admin shares in Templates, added with one click, skills switched on. See docs/org-library.md.

🎧 Bots that talk back

Press the speaker on any reply, or switch a bot to read its answers out as they land — so you can listen to what ran overnight while you make breakfast. Hit call and it's a conversation: it hears you, tells you what it's doing while it works, and asks for approvals out loud.

Choose ElevenLabs, Fish Audio, Grok (xAI), built-in Mac voices, or a local Chatterbox server in an agent profile. Paste a cloud key once when needed, pick a voice, and every bot can talk. Give a bot its own voice and a channel stops sounding like one person.

For Grok, save your xAI API key in Settings → Connections, then choose Grok (xAI) and a voice under the bot’s Voice & alerts. It reuses that host-side key and returns MP3 audio for spoken replies and calls. Language is detected automatically from the reply text; quality varies outside xAI’s officially supported languages. This adds speech synthesis to the existing call flow; microphone transcription remains unchanged.

Also in the box: streaming replies with tool-run activity chips · dictation from the composer mic (on-device Apple speech recognition on macOS, Fish Audio speech-to-text on Windows and Linux, in the desktop app) · SupaMaus cursor mascots with role-aware expressions · screenshots of the bot's work folded into the transcript.

Powered By

Service Purpose
Claude · Codex · Grok The agents behind every bot, run through their local CLIs
Electron Desktop shells for macOS, Windows, and Ubuntu
React + Vite + Tailwind CSS The chat app UI and its build
Boat (boat.dev) Each bot's cloud computer · our sponsor
ModelGo (modelgo.ai) One API key for every model · our inference provider sponsor
Composio Connected apps — Gmail, Slack, GitHub, and more
Cua Driver Native computer use on your own machine
ElevenLabs · Fish Audio Hosted voices for bots that talk back
GitHub Sponsors One-time and monthly project support

How it works

Two processes. The app holds no transports of its own — it sends typed commands over HTTP and folds one SSE event stream into state. The harness server owns every agent process and normalizes each provider's native protocol into one canonical runtime event stream (logged per-thread as NDJSON).

flowchart LR
    subgraph app ["App — React + Tailwind (5199)"]
        UI[Chat UI · model picker · computer panel]
    end
    subgraph server ["Harness server (127.0.0.1:8799)"]
        REG[Driver registry] --> BUS[Event bus → SSE]
        BROKER[Permission broker]
    end
    subgraph agents ["Agents on your computer"]
        CL[claude CLI]
        CX[codex CLI]
        GR[grok CLI]
    end
    UI -- "HTTP commands" --> server
    BUS -- "one SSE stream" --> UI
    REG --> CL & CX & GR
    CL & CX & GR -- "permission requests" --> BROKER
    server -- "Boat API" --> BOAT[("Cloud computer<br/>boat.dev")]
    server -- "Composio Session" --> APPS[("Gmail · Slack · GitHub · …")]
Layer Where What it does
Drivers server/drivers/ One per provider: Claude, Codex, and Grok Build over their local CLIs (stream-JSON / JSON-RPC / ACP), plus a cloud-computer agent. Unknown drivers degrade to "unavailable", never crash the fleet.
Harness server/harness/ Registry (configs → live instances) and the fan-in event bus every client folds.
API server/index.ts Bots, turns, approvals, model catalog, computer lifecycle, connectors, config — HTTP + SSE.
Voice server/tts/ ElevenLabs, Fish Audio, Grok (xAI), built-in Mac voices, or local Chatterbox. Cloud keys stay on the harness; markdown is rewritten into something worth hearing before it is spoken.
App src/ The chat shell. Server-backed store, one reducer, zero client-side transports.
Desktop electron/ macOS, Windows, and Ubuntu shells with an embedded harness and platform capabilities; Apple speech stays macOS-only, Ubuntu Xorg has opt-in local control, and Wayland remains fail-closed.

Orchestrate OpenMausBot over MCP

OpenMausBot ships a stdio MCP server for external clients such as Claude Desktop and Cursor. It exposes a deliberately bounded team control plane: inspect bots and channels, read/search compact transcript pages, create and configure bots/channels/tasks, send work, wait for completion, switch models, and interrupt turns. It does not expose approval grants, deletion, arbitrary settings, credentials, or computer lifecycle.

See MCP server setup and tool reference.

Run it from scripts and CI

The openmausbot command drives a running workspace without a screen: set a team up from a file, give a bot one job, wait until it and every teammate it asked are done, and export what they made. One JSON document with --json, and exit codes a script can branch on.

openmausbot team apply team.yaml
openmausbot run "Room Lead" "Rehearse the launch of https://example.com" --export ./out

See Run OpenMausBot from scripts and CI.

Quick start

Released builds (latest release): the harness server is embedded, so no separate server setup is required.

Download Install
macOS (Apple silicon) OpenMausBot.dmg Drag it to Applications, open it. Signed & notarized.
macOS (Intel) OpenMausBot-intel.dmg Same app, built for Intel Macs. Signed & notarized.
Windows (x64) OpenMausBot-setup.exe Run it — one-click, per-user, no admin rights. The installer isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen shows "unknown publisher": More info → Run anyway. By default the app installs to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\OpenMausBot, and every update goes back to the folder the installer recorded, so keep it where the installer put it: a copy moved by hand (for example from C: to D:) is left behind, and the next update lands in the recorded folder again.
Ubuntu 24.04 (x64) OpenMausBot-amd64.deb · OpenMausBot.AppImage Install the .deb with APT (recommended), or make the AppImage executable and run it. Beta; GNOME is the supported desktop.
Fedora (x64) OpenMausBot-x86_64.rpm Install with sudo dnf install ./OpenMausBot-x86_64.rpm. Community-supported; Ubuntu is the tested Linux.

See the Ubuntu Desktop guide for installation, capabilities, and troubleshooting. Any desktop build can also open the bots of another Windows, macOS, or Ubuntu computer over Tailscale; see open one computer's bots from another computer.

From source:

git clone https://github.com/milind-soni/OpenMausBot && cd OpenMausBot
pnpm install

pnpm dev:server    # harness server → 127.0.0.1:8799
pnpm dev           # app → http://127.0.0.1:5199
pnpm dev:desktop   # Electron shell; keep the two commands above running

Requirements: macOS, Windows, or Ubuntu 24.04 x64, Node 24+, pnpm, and at least one agent CLI — claude, codex, or grok — installed and logged in. They appear in the model picker automatically.

Package the desktop application:

pnpm package:mac      # macOS: DMG + ZIP; requires Swift/Xcode tools
pnpm package:win      # Windows: installer + ZIP
pnpm package:linux    # Linux x64: .deb + .rpm + AppImage + verified CUA runtime

Desktop capability status

Capability macOS Windows x64 Ubuntu 24.04 Xorg Ubuntu 24.04 Wayland
Packaged app, embedded harness, local agent CLIs Supported Supported Beta Beta
Composio and Boat/cloud computers Supported Supported Beta Beta
Explicit preview-only local screen capture Supported Unavailable Beta Beta
Bot control of this computer Supported Supported Beta, explicit opt-in Disabled: Wayland safety gate (Omarchy with Cua's Hyprland plugin: experimental)
Native on-device dictation Supported Unavailable Planned Planned
Dictation and Take turns calls through Fish Audio (needs a Fish Audio key) Not used, on-device instead Supported Supported Supported

On Windows, choose This computer to let a bot control the local desktop. The packaged app includes its own CUA driver and SDK; a separate Cua installation is not required. Local bot control is available even though the preview-only screen capture above is unavailable. See Computer use & browser use.

The Linux preview is user-initiated and never enables local bot control or Auto routing. On Xorg, the reviewed Cua Driver 0.41.3 runtime starts only after explicit opt-in and without its full-screen cursor overlay. On Wayland the app never starts it and clears legacy opt-ins while that real-seat safety gate remains unresolved. Chat, preview, Cloud, and Local VM remain available on both sessions. See the Ubuntu Desktop guide and tracking issues #29, #345, and #113.

The Linux packager downloads only the tag-pinned upstream archive during the build, verifies its size, SHA-256, complete member allowlist, and inner executable hashes, then packages only the CLI and cursor-theme sidecar. The installed app never downloads or self-updates native automation code. Cua's MIT notice, Inter's SIL OFL, a generated third-party license report, and a CycloneDX inventory ship with the runtime. See third_party/cua-driver/ for the reviewed provenance record.

These credentials are optional — local chat works without them. Paste a key once in App Settings (gear in the sidebar footer) when you want to enable its integration:

Credential What it enables Where to get it
Composio project key (ak_…) Connect Gmail, GitHub, Slack, Notion, and other apps to your bots OpenMausBot Composio setup
Boat API key Give bots an isolated remote Linux computer with a desktop and terminal Boat API key guide
ElevenLabs key Read replies aloud, and call your bots ElevenLabs API keys
Fish Audio key Read replies aloud with Fish Audio voices, and call your bots Fish Audio API keys

Composio and Boat are third-party services with their own accounts and terms. Boat is a paid service after its trial, and using a cloud computer may incur charges.

pnpm typecheck     # app + server
pnpm test          # unit, driver, API, and desktop capability tests
pnpm build         # typecheck + production build
pnpm check:electron # syntax-check Electron main/preload files
pnpm package:win   # Windows installer + zip → release/
pnpm package:linux # Linux x64 .deb + .rpm + AppImage → release/

Triggers: schedules and webhooks

A trigger is "when something happens, a bot does something". Tell a bot "every weekday at 9, send me a summary of my inbox" or "whenever our form calls, draft a reply" and it sets the trigger up in that turn with its trigger tool (no confirmation; the chat shows a live card with Edit, Pause and Undo). Triggers, first in the sidebar, lists every schedule and webhook, with a calendar and the run history. Bots manage them with trigger_info (list, app events), trigger (create, update, pause, resume, run now) and delete_trigger; a webhook a bot makes never shows the bot its secret: the person copies the link from the card or the Triggers page.

Schedules (routines) can run once, on selected weekdays, or every 5–1,440 minutes, using either a bot's configured model/computer or the Cloud VM runner. Interval schedules stay aligned to their chosen start time and skip an occurrence when the previous run is still active, so slow work cannot build an unbounded queue. A separate optional Advanced run limit can safely stop stuck work; no timeout is imposed unless one is chosen. The existing duration field remains calendar/display metadata. Webhook triggers are independent from schedules but reuse the same queued task executor and calendar receipts.

App events start a bot when something happens in a connected app ("whenever I get an email from Acme, draft a reply"). The bot finds the app's events with trigger_info (action: "events") and calls trigger with action: "create" and when: "app_event"; the person can also choose New → Set it up yourself → When something happens in an app. Composio sends each event to OpenMausBot's connected-apps service, which queues it; the app collects the queue with a long poll, so a desktop needs no public address and events wait while it is closed. Gmail is checked every 15 minutes; Slack, GitHub and other push apps arrive at once. A desktop keeps up to 500 events a day and a paid Cloud 2,000; what is skipped shows on the automation. App events need the included connected apps: a server using its own Composio key cannot watch apps yet. Details: docs/composio.md.

OpenMausBot starts a webhook-only receiver on 127.0.0.1:8800 by default (or one port above OMB_PORT). Set OMB_WEBHOOK_PORT to choose another port. A webhook secret is shown once when the trigger is created or rotated. Bearer authentication is recommended so the secret stays out of request URLs and most access logs; a single capability URL remains available for senders that cannot configure headers. The receiver exposes only /health and secret /hooks/... endpoints; it never exposes the app's broader API. OpenMausBot must remain running to accept a delivery. For public internet delivery, proxy only this dedicated receiver through a hosted relay or a tool such as Tailscale Funnel.

Status

Early but real — the loop works end to end: message → agent → streamed reply → tools → approvals → computer use. macOS, Windows, and Ubuntu 24.04 x64 have released builds; Ubuntu remains a beta with the capability limits above. Rough edges to expect: hosted/mobile connectivity is still being built, and webhook triggers currently use the local receiver rather than an always-on hosted relay. Hosted voice needs an ElevenLabs, Fish Audio, or xAI key; built-in Mac and local Chatterbox voices need no cloud key. Take-turns calls and the composer mic listen on-device on macOS and through Fish Audio speech-to-text on Windows and Linux (the same Fish Audio key as voices). See docs/voice-mode.md for the design and the known gaps.

Contributions welcome — the driver SPI in server/contracts.ts is deliberately small; adding a provider is one file in server/drivers/ plus a one-line registration. No code needed at all for your own engines: any ACP-speaking CLI or OpenAI-compatible endpoint plugs in through config — see docs/custom-engines.md. Users can add their own MCP tool servers with zero code via docs/custom-mcp-servers.md. For configuration switches, defaults and model-call implications, see Feature switches. To run bots on OpenRouter, Fireworks AI, DeepSeek, Cline or your own OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible provider, see Other model providers.

Privacy

Usage analytics are optional and anonymous: product events and a once-a-day count of what is set up, never keys, names, addresses or conversations. Turn them off in Settings → General → Usage analytics; docs/analytics.md lists every event and property.

Support the project

OpenMausBot is free and open source. If it does real work for you, you can support its development through GitHub Sponsors with a one-time contribution or a monthly sponsorship. Your support helps fund ongoing development and maintenance; OpenMausBot remains free and open source.

Run from a terminal or on a server

With Node 24 or newer, install once and run:

npm install -g openmausbot
openmausbot

Or use npx openmausbot without a global install. First launch guides you with arrow-key choices: choose AI access, sign in or paste a hidden API key, choose a model, and optionally connect a phone. Next time, the same command reuses your saved setup and opens OpenMausBot on this computer. Keep the terminal open; Ctrl-C stops the server, not your saved work. Use --no-open to skip opening the browser.

Phone access is optional and defaults to skipping. Choose an explicitly approved managed public HTTPS endpoint protected by pairing, an existing Tailscale connection, or your own HTTPS reverse proxy. Both native apps pair from this flow: the QR is an app link when you are connecting an Android phone, and the iOS app takes either that or the web link. A browser works on either phone. A phone cannot use a localhost link. --local ignores saved remote access for one launch; --no-pair suppresses phone prompts and invitations but does not disable a saved remote connection.

The web UI can also be installed from Safari or Chrome as a standalone phone app. See Install the phone web app for Home Screen installation and pairing.

Run openmausbot setup to reconfigure without resetting bots or conversations; the saved model default applies only to new bots. Native setup confirms provider sign-in; API setup asks before a potentially billable test message. API keys from openmausbot setup and the server are saved as plaintext, not encrypted, in private config.json (0600 on Unix). The packaged desktop app keeps your AI provider and service keys encrypted through the operating system instead; its config.json still holds OpenCode provider keys, keys given to one engine, and MCP header values in plaintext (a key a bot set from a secret card is kept in the Vault, and config.json holds only a pointer to it). See the short setup guide for account differences, phone choices, credential storage, and cancellation.

For a server on a VPS or an always-on computer, run npx openmausbot serve with one way in: --public-url behind your own cloudflared, Caddy or nginx, --domain for a certificate on your own domain, --tailscale for your tailnet, --lan for this network only, or --tunnel (after npx openmausbot account login) for a free MausBot web address. It prints one pairing link; paste it into the desktop app under ＋ → Connect to a server. The short path for each install method (npx, Docker, a service) is at the top of docs/self-hosting.md; a server from scratch is docs/deploy-vps.md.

License

Apache License 2.0 © 2026 Milind Soni and OpenMausBot contributors, except enterprise/, which is source-available under its own license; delete that folder and what remains is the open-source edition. Details, including how contributions are signed off, are in LICENSING.md.

Packaged Cua Driver components retain their upstream MIT, SIL OFL 1.1, MPL-2.0, and other dependency terms; the corresponding notices, license texts, source locations, and SBOM are in third_party/cua-driver/ and ship beside the native runtime.

OpenMausBot is an independent, open-source project inspired by Grok Bot. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or associated with xAI; "Grok" is a trademark of its respective owner.

item.title: Viren070/AIOStreams
item.description:
AIOStreams brings your Stremio addons, debrid services and Usenet together into one list, filtered, sorted and formatted your way, and plays it in Stremio or in its own apps for every screen.

https://aiostreams.org/

AIOStreams

One addon for all your sources, and the apps to watch them in.

AIOStreams brings your Stremio addons, debrid services and Usenet together into one list, filtered, sorted and formatted your way, and plays it in Stremio or in its own apps for every screen.

Docs · Public instances · Download the app · Changelog · Discord

What it does

Instead of juggling a dozen addons, each with its own settings and its own way of listing results, you configure AIOStreams once. It asks every source you've added, removes the duplicates, filters, sorts and names what comes back by your rules, and hands you one clean list, wherever you watch.

flowchart LR
  subgraph Sources
    A["Stremio addons<br/>80+ in the marketplace, or any by URL"]
    B["Built-in addons<br/>torrent and Usenet indexers, SeaDex…"]
    C["Debrid and Usenet services<br/>Real-Debrid, TorBox, Easynews…"]
  end
  P{{"AIOStreams<br/>dedupe · filter · sort · format"}}
  subgraph Watch["Where you watch"]
    E["Stremio<br/>as an addon"]
    F["The AIOStreams app<br/>browser, desktop, Android, TVs"]
    G["Jellyfin apps<br/>Infuse, Swiftfin, Findroid, Kodi…"]
  end
  A & B & C --> P --> E & F & G

Everything here works on a public instance. Host your own and you also get a Usenet engine and more.

🎛️ Your rules

Because every source goes through AIOStreams, you set your rules once and they apply to every addon.

  • Filters by resolution, quality, encode, HDR and Dolby Vision, audio, language, size, bitrate, seeders, age, cache status, keywords and regular expressions, with matching that checks titles, years and episodes so you only see the right file.
  • Sorting by any stack of criteria, separately for movies, series and anime and for cached and uncached results, with ranked preferences and scores.
  • Deduplication by file name, info hash, or a fingerprint of the file's details.
  • Stream expressions for rules that depend on the whole list, such as dropping 720p only when there's enough 1080p.
  • A formatter that names each stream the way you want, with a live preview and ready-made formats to start from.
  • Catalogs renamed, reordered, merged, shuffled or hidden, with better posters from services like RPDB.
  • Groups that ask backup addons only when the main ones come up short, and variants that serve several differently tuned addons from one configuration.
  • Templates to start from a complete setup someone shared, and profiles to reopen yours by signing in.

🔌 Sources

  • Addon marketplace: 80+ community addons (Torrentio, Comet, MediaFusion and many more) to enable in a click, or add any Stremio addon by URL. Streams, catalogs, metadata and subtitles are all supported.
  • Built-in addons that run inside AIOStreams: torrent and Usenet indexers, Prowlarr, Jackett, NZBHydra2, Newznab and Torznab, SeaDex for anime, Xtream for your IPTV provider's channels, Google Drive, and your debrid or Usenet library.
  • Services entered once and applied to every addon that can use them: Real-Debrid, AllDebrid, TorBox, Premiumize, Debrid-Link, put.io, Offcloud, PikPak, EasyDebrid and more for debrid; Easynews, NzbDAV, AltMount, Stremio NNTP and StremThru Newz for Usenet.
The built-in addons
Addon What it finds
Knaben A meta-search across The Pirate Bay, 1337x, Nyaa and more
The Pirate Bay The Pirate Bay, by title and IMDb ID
TheRARBG TheRARBG, by title and IMDb ID
Torrent Galaxy Torrent Galaxy
EZTV TV shows on EZTV
Zilean A Zilean DMM hashlist instance
Bitmagnet Your self-hosted Bitmagnet DHT crawler
SeaDex The community's best releases for anime
AnimeTosho Most Nyaa and TokyoTosho anime releases
NekoBT Anime releases on nekoBT
Tsukihime Anime releases, matched by MAL and AniDB ID
Prowlarr, Jackett Your indexer manager
NZBHydra2 Your Usenet indexers, through NZBHydra2
Newznab, Torznab Any Newznab (Usenet) or Torznab (torrent) indexer
Easynews Search Easynews' Usenet index
Xtream Your IPTV provider's channels, programme guide and catch-up, from your Xtream login
Stremio GDrive Your Google Drive
Library What's already in your debrid or Usenet library

Built-in addons that search torrents need a debrid service. Every built-in addon that searches supports anime and Kitsu and MAL catalogs.

📺 Watch anywhere

In Stremio

Install AIOStreams as one addon in place of the rest, in Stremio or any app that supports Stremio addons. Link your Stremio account and changes you save reinstall themselves.

In the AIOStreams app

Your catalogs become a streaming app of AIOStreams' own, and your streams become versions of each title, sorted and named by your rules. There's nothing extra to host: every configuration is also a media server, so the app signs in to it, and so does any Jellyfin app. Download it for your computer, phone or TV.

Where App Plays with
Any browser Nothing to install: your instance's /web or web.aiostreams.org, which a phone can add to its home screen A WebGPU engine: HEVC, Dolby Vision, TrueHD and DTS, audio tracks, styled subtitles
Windows, macOS, Linux Desktop app mpv: nearly any format, HDR, surround passthrough, styled subtitles
Android phones and tablets Android app ExoPlayer or mpv: HDR and Dolby Vision, passthrough, styled subtitles
Android TV, Google TV, Fire TV Android app, with a layout made for the remote ExoPlayer or mpv
LG and Samsung TVs (beta) TV apps, installed from a file The TV's own player
iPhone, iPad, Apple TV, Kodi… A browser, or any Jellyfin app such as Infuse or Swiftfin The app's own player

The apps play streams with a link, such as debrid and Usenet ones; P2P torrents stay in Stremio.

It works as it comes. The player needs no setting up:

  • Styled subtitles, such as most anime releases, drawn by libass in every app, signs and all, in a browser and on TVs too.
  • Dolby Vision and HDR, with profile 7 converted where a device only plays profile 8.
  • Surround sound passed through to your receiver format by format, or turned into Dolby Digital for an optical or ARC link, and the TV switched to each video's frame rate.
  • Subtitles from your addons synced to the video by themselves, or by ear, or by picking the spoken line.
  • Seek previews, skipped intros and credits, and the next episode on its own.
  • Anime upscaling in the desktop and Android apps and the browser's WebGPU engine, which sharpens older and lower-resolution anime as it plays.

It runs on your addons. Catalogs, details, ratings, streams, subtitles and Live TV all come from addons. Tracker addons that support Watch State bring in your history, watchlist and ratings, and get your progress, ratings and drops back as you watch.

  • Browse a home page with a featured title, rows for Continue Watching, Next Up and each catalog, Discover, search, collections, favourites, a calendar of airing episodes, trailers, and a page for every title and person.
  • Live TV from IPTV addons or your Xtream login, with channel groups and numbers, a programme guide with the channel playing above it, catch-up and reminders.
  • Versions are your streams. Search them, save quick filters, label them with badges, switch mid-play, or open one in VLC, Infuse or another player.
  • Households get a user each, with their own Continue Watching and an optional PIN; TVs sign in with a Quick Connect code.
  • Watch together in sync with friends, on your server or across servers, with chat and reactions.
  • Play on another device turns the app into a remote for a TV or computer running it.
  • Playlists, a mini player that keeps playing while you browse, and downloads for offline viewing on desktop and Android.
  • Make it yours: navigation along the top, down the side or in a corner on solid, frosted or liquid glass, themes and your own colours, and custom CSS with hooks on every part of the app. The apps are in your language too, translated on Weblate.

Elsewhere

From the same page you can also add AIOStreams to Seanime, Chillio and Aniyomi, or query it through the search API.

🏠 On your own instance

Hosting AIOStreams yourself (or on a private ElfHosted instance) adds what a public instance can't offer.

  • A built-in Usenet engine. Give it your NNTP provider and it streams releases straight from Usenet, archives included, with no NzbDAV, AltMount or SABnzbd in between. In the public Usenet streaming benchmark, which runs nine applications over the same releases, it is first to the first byte and first to finish a seek. Usenet guide.
  • Sonarr and Radarr can use the engine as their SABnzbd download client: they grab as usual, and Plex, Jellyfin or Emby stream the release from Usenet on demand, a library that takes no disk space. AIOStreams can also be their Newznab and Torznab indexer.
  • A release blocklist that remembers dead and fake releases, drops them before they're tried, and can be shared between instances.
  • A dashboard for the instance: live streams and bandwidth, analytics, logs, users, the Usenet library and providers, cache, tasks, crash reports from the apps, and every runtime setting.
  • Accounts from AIOSTREAMS_AUTH or any OpenID Connect provider through SSO, with per-user permissions, on SQLite or PostgreSQL, with Redis for several replicas.
  • Proxies: the built-in proxy, MediaFlow Proxy or StremThru, for services that limit how many IPs can stream.

🚀 Getting started

  1. Pick an instance

    • A public instance: free, nothing to set up.

    • Your own:

      curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Viren070/AIOStreams/main/compose.yaml
curl -o .env https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Viren070/AIOStreams/main/.env.sample
# set SECRET_KEY in .env (a 64-character hex string), then:
docker compose up -d

    • Managed hosting from ElfHosted, a project sponsor.

  2. Configure it at /stremio/configure: add your services, pick addons and set your rules, or import a template to start from a complete setup.
  3. Save with a password.
  4. Install or open it from Save & Install: in Stremio, in the AIOStreams app, in a Jellyfin app, or in any of the other apps listed there.

The documentation covers every option, environment variable and guide.

❤️ Support the project

AIOStreams is built and maintained for free. If it's useful to you:

  • ⭐ Star the repository, and the addon in the Stremio Community Catalog.
  • 🌍 Translate the apps into your language.
  • 🤝 Report bugs, suggest features or open a pull request.
  • ☕ Donate on Ko-fi or GitHub Sponsors.

⭐ Star history

⚠️ Disclaimer

AIOStreams does not host, store or distribute any content. It connects to the sources you configure (addons, debrid services and Usenet providers) and plays what they return. The developer does not endorse or promote access to copyrighted content. You are responsible for complying with the laws that apply to you and with the terms of every service you use with AIOStreams.

🙏 Credits

AIOStreams builds on the work of many others, especially the developers of the addons it integrates.

  • mpv, FFmpeg, libass and Media3 ExoPlayer, which the apps play video with, and WebGPU-Player and JASSUB, which play video and draw subtitles in a browser.
  • Jellyfin, whose API the media server speaks.
  • mhdzumair/mediaflow-proxy and MunifTanjim/stremthru.
  • UI components and issue templates adapted with permission from 5rahim/seanime.
  • NzbDAV and AltMount support, inspired by Sanket9225/UsenetStreamer.
  • sleeyax/stremio-easynews-addon, the project's initial structure.
  • The formatter, inspired by and adapted from diced/zipline.
  • The Stream Expression Language, powered by silentmatt/expr-eval, via the patched jorenbroekema/expr-eval fork.

LobeHub

Super-Agents on Your Team

Add super-agents to the chats your team already uses.
They take on work by themselves and get better every week.

English · 简体中文 · Official Site · Changelog · Documents · Blog · Feedback




Share LobeHub Repository

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a33365f-b786-48b5-9ed6-f8af7927bccb

👋🏻 Getting Started & Join Our Community

We are a group of e/acc design-engineers, hoping to provide modern design components and tools for AIGC.

Whether for users or professional developers, LobeHub will be your AI Agent playground. Please be aware that LobeHub is currently under active development, and feedback is welcome for any issues encountered.

We are live on Product Hunt! We are thrilled to bring LobeHub to the world. If you believe in a future where humans and agents co-evolve, please support our journey.
Join our Discord community! This is where you can connect with developers and other enthusiastic users of LobeHub.

Important

Star Us, You will receive all release notifications from GitHub without any delay ~ ⭐️

Star History

✨ Features

From new hire to one of the team

See what Lobe AI gets done, from its first day in your team chat onward.

WHAT MAKES A SUPER-AGENT

🔌 Flexible access
Plug in any IM app, agent or model, all in one place. 		⚡ Parallel work
Runs several tasks at once, so you don't have to chase each one.
🙋 Finds its own work
Takes on the tasks that suit it, without someone passing messages along. 		📈 Gets more expert
The more you use it, the faster an agent builds up its expertise.

Day 1 Welcome to the team

You add it to your team chat and ask it to read up. By lunch it has gone through the history and said hello to everyone.

Week 1 Its first task

Someone posts a feature request in Discord and nobody assigns it. Lobe AI takes it on, and you only step in once, to accept the result.

Month 1–2 Settling in as the team grows

Everyone now has their own agent, and design, releases and docs each have a dedicated one. Lobe AI is still learning when to speak up and when to stay quiet.

Month 3 It passes its review

When it started, it got about half of these right. Now it rarely misses, and every correction you gave it has become a lesson it keeps.

Bring them onto your team

Start with one, and add more when you need them.

Try LobeHub Cloud · Self-host it

Contact: business@lobehub.com

🧩 Marketplace

Find agents, MCP servers and skills on lobehub.com, add them to your workspace, or publish your own.

Market What you'll find
🤖 Agents Ready-to-use agents for writing, Q&A, images, video, voice and workflows. Add one to your workspace and adapt it.
🔌 MCP Servers MCP servers rated on activity, stability and community feedback, so you can pick ones you can trust.
🧠 Skills Agent skills in the open SKILL.md format. They also work in Claude Code, Codex CLI and ChatGPT.
🎨 AI / LLM Icons A free icon set for major AI brands and models, with SVG, PNG and vector downloads.

Publish your own

  • Agents: submit one from its settings in LobeHub. The Creator Reward Program features a community agent every two weeks.

  • MCP servers: ask your agent to Read https://lobehub.com/publish-mcp/skill.md and follow the instructions to publish my MCP server to the LobeHub Marketplace, or use the CLI:

    npx -y @lobehub/market-cli login
npx -y @lobehub/market-cli plugin submit https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY

  • Skills: submit a GitHub repository from the Skills marketplace.

📖 Documentation

All documentation lives at lobehub.com/docs:

Section What's covered
Get LobeHub Web, macOS, Windows, Linux and mobile apps, and where work runs
Lobe AI The built-in agent: chat, code, research and write with no setup
Agents System role, model, skills, connectors, web search, resources and memory
Agent Team Several agents working together: sequential, parallel, iterative or debate
Connect External Agents Bring in Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes and more, with project context and permissions
Tasks Delegate work, track status, follow up in comments, run once or on a schedule
Memory Structured memories you can review, edit and delete
Pages Write long documents with agents, in Markdown
Resource Library Documents, generated images and drafts your agents can answer from
Channels Your own bots on Discord, Slack, Telegram, LINE, QQ, WeChat, Feishu and Lark
Messenger Chat with your agents through LobeHub's bot on Telegram, Slack, Discord and WeChat
GitHub Integration Track agents' pull requests; merging accepts the work, failed checks go back to the agent
Marketplace Community agents, MCP servers and skills
Model Providers Setup guides for 40+ providers, inference platforms and local models
Self-Hosting Docker Compose, Vercel and other deployment platforms
Environment Variables Every configuration option, including model providers
Authentication Sign-in with Better Auth and SSO providers such as Auth0
Development Tech stack, local setup and contribution guidelines

🛳 Self Hosting

Run LobeHub on your own infrastructure and keep your data with you. The full guide is in 📘 Build your own LobeHub.

A Docker Compose (recommended)

Starts LobeHub with PostgreSQL, Redis, RustFS file storage, SearXNG search and the agent gateway. Runs on Linux and macOS, or on Windows through WSL 2.

mkdir lobehub && cd lobehub
bash <(curl -fsSL https://lobe.li/setup.sh) -l en
docker compose up -d

Then open http://localhost:3210. Ports, LAN and domain modes, and upgrades are covered in the 📘 Docker Compose guide.

B One-click deploy

Vercel needs a PostgreSQL database, S3-compatible storage and a few secrets before you deploy. The 📘 Vercel guide walks through each one.

Deploy with Vercel Deploy with Zeabur Deploy with Sealos Deploy with RepoCloud Deploy with Alibaba Cloud

⌨️ Local Development

You can use GitHub Codespaces for online development:

Or clone it for local development:

$ git clone https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub.git
$ cd lobehub
$ pnpm install
$ bun run dev       # Full-stack (Next.js + Vite SPA)
$ bun run dev:spa   # SPA frontend only (port 9876)

Debug Proxy: After running dev:spa, the terminal prints a proxy URL like https://app.lobehub.com/_dangerous_local_dev_proxy?debug-host=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A9876. Open it to develop locally against the production backend with HMR — a development convenience, not a place to verify a change.

If you would like to learn more details, please feel free to look at our 📘 Development Guide.

🤝 Contributing

Contributions of all types are more than welcome; if you are interested in contributing code, feel free to check out our GitHub Issues and Projects to get stuck in to show us what you're made of.

Tip

We are creating a technology-driven forum, fostering knowledge interaction and the exchange of ideas that may culminate in mutual inspiration and collaborative innovation.

Help us make LobeHub better. Welcome to provide product design feedback, user experience discussions directly to us.

Principal Maintainers: @arvinxx @canisminor1990

❤️ Sponsor

Every bit counts and your one-time donation sparkles in our galaxy of support! You're a shooting star, making a swift and bright impact on our journey. Thank you for believing in us – your generosity guides us toward our mission, one brilliant flash at a time.

🔬 Research

  • 📊 MCPMark: A stress-testing benchmark for MCP. Its tasks are realistic, multi-step and verifiable, covering file systems, databases, Playwright browser automation, GitHub and more. Built by EVAL SYS, LobeHub and the National University of Singapore, and open source under Apache-2.0.
